docs.title: QUASAR - AI-Powered CLI Code Editor
docs.text:
🚀 Your Intelligent Coding Assistant in the Terminal

QUASAR is an AI-powered command-line code editor that can understand your codebase, generate code, fix bugs, and execute tasks using AI.

docs.title: ✨ Features
docs.text:
• :material-robot: Intelligent AI Agent

    Understands context, plans tasks, and executes with 27+ tools

  • :material-server: Multiple Providers

    Supports Groq, Cerebras, and local Ollama models

  • :material-cog: MCP Integration

    Extend capabilities with Model Context Protocol servers

  • :material-hook: Custom Hooks

    Add your own lifecycle hooks for custom behavior

  • :material-backup-restore: Auto Backup

    Automatic file backups before every modification

  • :material-shield-lock: Secure

    Blocks access to sensitive files like .env and SSH keys

docs.title: 🚀 Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install QUASAR
pip install quasar-ai

# Set your API key
export GROQ_API_KEY_1="gsk_your_key_here"

# Run QUASAR
quasar "create a hello.py file that prints Hello World"

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for QUASAR command-line options.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: quasar [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PROMPT Your request to QUASAR

docs.title: --workspace / -w
docs.text:
Specify the working directory.

quasar --workspace /path/to/project "your request"

Default: Current directory (.)

docs.title: --model / -m
docs.text:
Specify provider and model.

quasar --model provider/model-name "your request"

Format: provider/model-name

Examples:

quasar --model cerebras/zai-glm-4.7 "create hello.py"
quasar --model groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b "explain main.py"
quasar --model ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b "fix bug"

Default: Auto (Cerebras → Ollama → Groq)

docs.title: --interactive / -i
docs.text:
Enter interactive REPL mode.

quasar --interactive
quasar -i

Interactive mode allows multiple commands without restarting.

docs.title: --version / -v
docs.text:
Show version information.

quasar --version

Output:

QUASAR v2.0.0 (or higher)

docs.title: --help / -h
docs.text:
Show help message.

quasar --help

docs.title: Single Command
docs.text:
# Create a file
quasar "create a hello.py that prints Hello World"

# Explain code
quasar "explain what main.py does"

# Search
quasar "find all files with TODO comments"

docs.title: With Options
docs.text:
# Specify workspace
quasar -w /projects/myapp "add tests"

# Use specific model
quasar -m groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b "refactor api.py"

# Both options
quasar -w /projects/myapp -m cerebras/zai-glm-4.7 "optimize queries"

docs.title: Interactive Mode
docs.text:
quasar -i
> explain main.py
> add error handling
> create tests
> exit

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Error 130 User interrupt (Ctrl+C)

docs.title: Backup & Recovery
docs.text: QUASAR automatically backs up files before modifying them.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Edit Request → Backup Original → Apply Changes → Success

Every time QUASAR modifies a file:

  1. Backup: Original saved to .quasar/backups/
  2. Modify: Changes applied to file
  3. Confirm: Success reported

docs.title: Backup Location
docs.text:
.quasar/
└── backups/
    ├── main.py.backup.2024-02-08T10-30-00
    ├── config.py.backup.2024-02-08T10-35-15
    └── utils.py.backup.2024-02-08T11-00-22

Filename format: {original}.backup.{timestamp}

docs.title: List Backups
docs.text:
Ask QUASAR:

> list backups for main.py

Or use the tool directly:

# From QUASAR's tools
list_backups("main.py")

docs.title: Restore Backup
docs.text:
Ask QUASAR:

> restore main.py from last backup

Or specify a timestamp:

> restore main.py from backup 2024-02-08T10-30-00

docs.title: View Diff
docs.text:
Compare current with backup:

> show diff for main.py vs last backup

QUASAR will show:

- old line
+ new line
  unchanged line

docs.title: Automatic Behavior
docs.text: Action Backup Created? create_file ❌ No (new file) modify_file ✅ Yes patch_file ✅ Yes delete_file ✅ Yes move_file ✅ Yes

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
By default, backups are retained indefinitely. To clean up:

# Manual cleanup
rm -rf .quasar/backups/*

# Or ask QUASAR
> delete backups older than 7 days

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Before Major Changes

QUASAR creates backups automatically, but for major refactors, consider using git: 

git add -A && git commit -m "backup before refactor"

Check Backups

Periodically review your backups folder size: 

du -sh .quasar/backups/

docs.title: Model Selection
docs.text: QUASAR supports multiple AI models from different providers.

docs.title: Auto Mode (Default)
docs.text:
By default, QUASAR automatically selects the best model:

quasar "your request"

Priority Order:

  1. Cerebras - Best for tool calling
  2. Ollama - Local fallback
  3. Groq - Cloud fallback

docs.title: Manual Selection
docs.text:
Use --model to specify a model:

quasar --model provider/model-name "your request"

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Cerebras
quasar --model cerebras/zai-glm-4.7 "create a hello.py"

# Groq
quasar --model groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b "explain main.py"

# Ollama (local)
quasar --model ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b "fix the bug"

docs.title: Cerebras
docs.text: Model Description zai-glm-4.7 Default, balanced qwen-3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507 Large, powerful

docs.title: Groq
docs.text: Model Description openai/gpt-oss-120b Best for tools openai/gpt-oss-20b Smaller, faster llama-3.3-70b-versatile General purpose

docs.title: Ollama
docs.text:
Model Description glm-4.7:cloud Default, balanced deepseek-v3.1:671b-cloud Code intelligence gpt-oss:120b-cloud Large, powerful qwen3-coder:480b-cloud Coding focused

Custom Models

Use --model ollama/your-model for any local model.

docs.title: Fallback Behavior
docs.text:
When using Auto mode:

  1. Tries primary model
  2. If fails (rate limit, error), tries next
  3. Continues until success or all fail

When using --model:

  • Uses only specified model
  • No fallback to others
  • Fails if model unavailable

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
Best for Tool Calling

Use cerebras/zai-glm-4.7 or groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b

For Privacy

Use ollama/ models for local processing

For Speed

Groq models are fastest for inference

docs.title: Security
docs.text: QUASAR includes security features to protect sensitive data.

docs.title: Sensitive File Blocking
docs.text:
QUASAR blocks access to sensitive files:

Pattern Description .env* Environment files *.pem SSL/TLS certificates *.key Private keys *_rsa, *_ecdsa SSH keys .git/config Git credentials credentials* Credential files secrets* Secret files *.gpg GPG encrypted .aws/* AWS credentials .ssh/* SSH directory

docs.title: What Happens?
docs.text:
When you try to read/write sensitive files:

> read .env file

⚠️ Access blocked: .env is a sensitive file

QUASAR will:

  1. Block the operation
  2. Report the blocked attempt
  3. Continue without accessing the file

docs.title: Command Suggestions
docs.text:
QUASAR suggests commands, not executes them:

> run npm install

💡 Suggested command:
npm install

(Copy and run this command yourself)

This prevents:

  • Accidental data loss
  • Unintended side effects
  • Security vulnerabilities

docs.title: Workspace Isolation
docs.text:
QUASAR operates within the specified workspace:

quasar --workspace /path/to/project "your request"
  • Cannot access files outside workspace
  • Cannot traverse up directories
  • Respects project boundaries

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Never Commit Secrets

Keep .env files in .gitignore: 

.env
.env.local
.env.*.local

Use Environment Variables

Set API keys as environment variables: 

export GROQ_API_KEY_1="gsk_..."

Review Before Running

Always review QUASAR's suggested commands before executing them.

docs.title: Task Types
docs.text: QUASAR classifies your requests into 6 task types, each with optimized tools.

docs.title: Task Categories
docs.text: Task Type Description Primary Tools file_operations Create, edit, delete files File + Search search Find files and content Search + File execution Run commands Terminal + File + Search web Web search and URLs Web + File + Search code_intelligence Analyze code Code Intel + File + Search chat General conversation All except Terminal

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
User Request → Task Classification → Tool Selection → Execution
  1. Classification: QUASAR analyzes your request
  2. Tool Selection: Assigns appropriate tools
  3. Execution: Runs tools to complete task

docs.title: file_operations
docs.text:
Creates, modifies, or deletes files.

Triggers:

  • "create a file..."
  • "add to config.py..."
  • "delete old.py..."
  • "refactor utils.py..."

Tools: FILE_TOOLS + SEARCH_TOOLS

docs.title: search
docs.text:
Finds files and searches content.

Triggers:

  • "find files with..."
  • "search for 'TODO'..."
  • "list all Python files..."

Tools: SEARCH_TOOLS + FILE_TOOLS

docs.title: execution
docs.text:
Suggests terminal commands.

Triggers:

  • "how do I run tests?"
  • "install dependencies..."
  • "start the server..."

Tools: TERMINAL_TOOLS + FILE_TOOLS + SEARCH_TOOLS

Safety

QUASAR suggests commands, not executes them directly.

docs.title: web
docs.text:
Searches the web and fetches URLs.

Triggers:

  • "search for Python best practices..."
  • "what is FastAPI?"
  • "fetch the README from..."

Tools: WEB_TOOLS + FILE_TOOLS + SEARCH_TOOLS

docs.title: code_intelligence
docs.text:
Analyzes and understands code.

Triggers:

  • "explain main.py..."
  • "find definition of..."
  • "show references to..."

Tools: CODE_INTELLIGENCE_TOOLS + FILE_TOOLS + SEARCH_TOOLS

docs.title: chat
docs.text:
General conversation and questions.

Triggers:

  • "what is..."
  • "explain..."
  • (anything not matching other types)

Tools: All except Terminal

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configure QUASAR with API keys and options.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text: QUASAR requires API keys from at least one provider. You can use multiple keys for automatic rotation on rate limits.

docs.title: Option 1: Using .env file (Recommended)
docs.text:
Create a .env file in your project directory:

# Groq (recommended - fast inference)
GROQ_API_KEY_1=gsk_your_key_here
GROQ_API_KEY_2=gsk_your_second_key_here

# Cerebras
CEREBRAS_API_KEY_1=csk_your_key_here
CEREBRAS_API_KEY_2=csk_your_second_key_here

# Ollama runs locally - no API key needed
# Default: http://localhost:11434

# Web Search (optional but recommended)
# QUASAR has multiple web tools with fallback support
# Get free key at: https://tavily.com
TAVILY_API_KEY=tvly_your_key_here

docs.title: Option 2: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Linux/macOSWindows (CMD)Windows (PowerShell) 
# Groq
export GROQ_API_KEY_1="gsk_your_key_here"
export GROQ_API_KEY_2="gsk_your_second_key_here"

# Cerebras
export CEREBRAS_API_KEY_1="csk_your_key_here"

# Temporary (current session only)
set GROQ_API_KEY_1=gsk_your_key_here
set CEREBRAS_API_KEY_1=csk_your_key_here

# Permanent (restart terminal after)
setx GROQ_API_KEY_1 "gsk_your_key_here"
setx CEREBRAS_API_KEY_1 "csk_your_key_here"

# Temporary (current session only)
$env:GROQ_API_KEY_1 = "gsk_your_key_here"
$env:CEREBRAS_API_KEY_1 = "csk_your_key_here"

# Permanent
[System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("GROQ_API_KEY_1", "gsk_your_key_here", "User")

docs.title: Get Free API Keys
docs.text: Provider Free Tier Link Groq ✅ Yes console.groq.com Cerebras ✅ Yes cloud.cerebras.ai Ollama ✅ Free (Local) ollama.ai Tavily ✅ Yes tavily.com

docs.title: Multiple Keys
docs.text:
You can add multiple keys per provider:

GROQ_API_KEY_1=gsk_first_key
GROQ_API_KEY_2=gsk_second_key
GROQ_API_KEY_3=gsk_third_key

Benefits:

  • Automatic rotation on rate limits
  • No interruptions during heavy usage
  • Seamless failover

docs.title: Provider Priority
docs.text:
QUASAR uses this default priority:

  1. Cerebras - Best for tool calling
  2. Ollama - Local, good fallback
  3. Groq - Fast, but tool calling issues with some models

You can override with --model flag:

quasar --model groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b "your request"

docs.title: Ollama Configuration
docs.text: QUASAR uses cloud models via Ollama for fast execution.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Install Ollama from ollama.ai
  2. Start the server: ollama serve
  3. Pull the required cloud models:
# Required for Auto mode
ollama pull glm-4.7:cloud
ollama pull deepseek-v3.1:671b-cloud
ollama pull qwen3-coder:480b-cloud

docs.title: Default Models
docs.text: Model Description glm-4.7:cloud Default, balanced deepseek-v3.1:671b-cloud Code intelligence gpt-oss:120b-cloud Large, powerful qwen3-coder:480b-cloud Coding focused

docs.title: Custom/Local Models
docs.text:
You can also use any local model with the --model flag:

# Use a custom local model
quasar --model ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b "your request"
quasar --model ollama/codellama:7b "your request"

Default Ollama URL: http://localhost:11434

pip install quasar-ai

  • rich - Terminal formatting
  • langchain - AI orchestration
  • langchain-groq, langchain-ollama - Provider integrations

quasar --version

docs.text:
To upgrade to the latest version:

pip install --upgrade quasar-ai

docs.title: Development Installation
docs.text:
For development or contributing:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Sunilk240/QUASAR.git
cd QUASAR/quasar-cli

# Install in development mode
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Python Version Error
docs.text:
ERROR: This package requires Python 3.10 or higher

Solution: Upgrade Python:

# Check your Python version
python --version

# Use pyenv or install Python 3.10+

docs.title: Permission Error
docs.text:
ERROR: Could not install packages due to an EnvironmentError

Solution: Use --user flag or virtual environment:

pip install --user quasar-ai

# Or use virtual environment (recommended)
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install quasar-ai

docs.text: QUASAR supports multiple AI providers for flexibility and reliability.

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text: Provider Type Best For Free Tier Cerebras Cloud Tool calling, reliability ✅ Groq Cloud Speed, throughput ✅ Ollama Local Privacy, offline use ✅

docs.title: Provider Priority
docs.text:
QUASAR automatically selects providers in this order:

1. Cerebras (best for tool calling)

If a provider fails or hits rate limits, QUASAR automatically falls back to the next.

docs.title: Cerebras
docs.text: Cerebras is the primary provider for QUASAR - best for tool calling and reliability.

docs.title: Get API Key
docs.text:
1. Go to cloud.cerebras.ai
  2. Sign up or log in
  3. Navigate to API Keys
  4. Create a new API key

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add to your .env file:

CEREBRAS_API_KEY_1=csk_your_key_here
CEREBRAS_API_KEY_2=csk_your_second_key_here

docs.title: Available Models
docs.text:
Model Description Tool Calling zai-glm-4.7 Primary, balanced ✅ Excellent qwen-3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507 Large, powerful ✅ Excellent

Recommended

zai-glm-4.7 is the default and recommended model.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Auto mode (Cerebras is primary)
quasar "your request"

# Force Cerebras
quasar --model cerebras/zai-glm-4.7 "your request"

docs.title: Why Cerebras?
docs.text: Feature Cerebras Others Tool Calling ✅ Excellent ⚠️ Variable Reliability ✅ High ⚠️ Variable Speed ✅ Fast ✅ Fast Context Length ✅ Large ✅ Large

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text:
Cerebras free tier includes:

  • Generous request limits
  • High token limits

Tip: Add multiple keys for heavy usage:

CEREBRAS_API_KEY_1=csk_first_key

docs.title: context.md
docs.text: The context.md file provides project-specific context to the AI.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
When QUASAR processes your requests, it reads context.md and includes it in every prompt. This helps the AI:

  • Understand your project structure
  • Follow your coding conventions
  • Know about important files
  • Respect your project rules

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
.quasar/
└── context.md    # ← Your project context

docs.title: Default Template
docs.text:
QUASAR creates a template when initializing:

# Project Context

## Description
[Describe your project here]

## Code Style
- [Your coding conventions]
- [Naming patterns]
- [Framework preferences]

## Important Files
- [Key files to know about]

## Common Commands
- [Frequently used commands]

## Project Rules
- [Things the AI should always do]
- [Things the AI should never do]

## Notes
- [Any other context]

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Here's a real-world example:

# Project Context

## Description
FastAPI backend for an e-commerce platform.

## Code Style
- Use type hints for all functions
- Follow PEP 8 strictly
- Use async/await for all API endpoints
- Prefer pydantic models over dictionaries

## Important Files
- `app/main.py` - FastAPI app entry point
- `app/core/config.py` - All configuration
- `app/models/` - SQLAlchemy models
- `app/api/` - API route handlers

## Common Commands
- `uvicorn app.main:app --reload` - Start dev server
- `pytest` - Run tests
- `alembic upgrade head` - Run migrations

## Project Rules
- Never modify migration files directly
- Always add docstrings to functions
- Use environment variables for secrets
- Keep endpoints under 50 lines

## Notes
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Auth: JWT tokens
- Deployment: Docker + Kubernetes

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
User Request → PromptBuilder reads context.md → AI receives context

The context is injected into the system prompt, so the AI sees it before your request.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
Be Specific

Vague: "Use good code style" Specific: "Use type hints, follow PEP 8, max 80 chars per line"

List Key Files

Helps the AI find important code quickly

Include Commands

AI can suggest correct commands for your project

Set Rules

Prevent common mistakes by listing what NOT to do

docs.title: Sharing Context
docs.text:
To share context.md with your team:

# .gitignore
.quasar/memory.json

docs.title: Hooks System
docs.text: QUASAR supports lifecycle hooks for custom behavior at key points.

docs.title: What are Hooks?
docs.text:
Hooks are Python functions that run at specific points in QUASAR's workflow:

  • Before/after tool execution
  • On errors
  • On task completion
  • Before sending responses

docs.title: Hook Points
docs.text: Hook Point When It Runs PRE_TOOL_USE Before any tool is called POST_TOOL_USE After any tool completes ON_ERROR When an error occurs ON_COMPLETE When task completes PRE_RESPONSE Before sending response to user

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
.quasar/
└── hooks/
    ├── example_hook.py.disabled    # Template (disabled)
    └── my_hook.py                  # Active hook

Files ending in .disabled are not loaded.

docs.title: 1. Create Hook File
docs.text:
Create .quasar/hooks/my_hook.py:

from services.agent.hooks import hook, HookPoint, HookResult

@hook(HookPoint.PRE_TOOL_USE)
def before_tool(context):
    """Runs before every tool call."""
    tool_name = context.get("tool_name")
    print(f"🔧 About to use: {tool_name}")

    return HookResult(allow=True)

docs.title: 2. Restart QUASAR
docs.text: Hooks are loaded on startup.

docs.title: Block Dangerous Operations
docs.text:
@hook(HookPoint.PRE_TOOL_USE)
def block_delete(context):
    """Block file deletions."""
    tool_name = context.get("tool_name")

    if tool_name == "delete_file":
        return HookResult(
            allow=False,
            message="⚠️ File deletion blocked by hook"
        )

    return HookResult(allow=True)

docs.title: Log All Tool Calls
docs.text:
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger("hook")

@hook(HookPoint.POST_TOOL_USE)
def log_tools(context):
    """Log all tool calls."""
    tool_name = context.get("tool_name")
    result = context.get("result")

    logger.info(f"Tool: {tool_name}")
    logger.info(f"Result: {result[:100]}...")

    return HookResult(allow=True)

docs.title: Notify on Errors
docs.text:
@hook(HookPoint.ON_ERROR)
def notify_error(context):
    """Send notification on errors."""
    error = context.get("error")

    # Send to Slack, email, etc.
    send_notification(f"QUASAR Error: {error}")

    return HookResult(allow=True)

docs.title: Modify Tool Arguments
docs.text:
@hook(HookPoint.PRE_TOOL_USE)
def auto_workspace(context):
    """Add workspace to all file operations."""
    tool_name = context.get("tool_name")
    args = context.get("args", {})

    if tool_name in ["create_file", "modify_file"]:
        # Add prefix to all paths
        if "path" in args:
            args["path"] = f"/workspace/{args['path']}"
            return HookResult(
                allow=True,
                modified_args=args
            )

    return HookResult(allow=True)

docs.title: HookResult
docs.text: Field Type Description allow bool If False, blocks the action modified_args dict Modified arguments to pass message str Message to log/display

docs.title: Async Hooks
docs.text:
Hooks can be async:

@hook(HookPoint.POST_TOOL_USE)
async def async_hook(context):
    """Async hook example."""
    await some_async_operation()
    return HookResult(allow=True)

docs.title: Enabling/Disabling
docs.text:
• Rename to .disabled to disable: 

    mv my_hook.py my_hook.py.disabled

  • Remove .disabled to enable: 

    mv my_hook.py.disabled my_hook.py

docs.title: MCP Integration
docs.text: QUASAR supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for extending capabilities.

docs.title: What is MCP?
docs.text: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard for connecting AI agents to external tools and services. QUASAR can load MCP servers to add new tools.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configure MCP servers in .quasar/mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "server-name": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "package-name"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text: Field Description command Executable to run (npx, python, etc.) args Command-line arguments env Environment variables (optional) cwd Working directory (optional, defaults to workspace) disabled Set to true to skip this server

docs.title: Example: DuckDuckGo Search
docs.text:
Add web search capability using DuckDuckGo:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "duckduckgo": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "duckduckgo-mcp-server"]
    }
  }
}

Then use it:

> search for "Python async tutorial"

docs.title: Simple Python MCP Server
docs.text:
Create .quasar/my_server.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Simple MCP Server - implements JSON-RPC protocol directly"""

import sys
import json
from datetime import datetime


def send_response(response: dict):
    """Send JSON-RPC response to stdout."""
    print(json.dumps(response), flush=True)


def handle_request(request: dict) -> dict:
    """Handle incoming JSON-RPC request."""
    method = request.get("method", "")
    params = request.get("params", {})
    request_id = request.get("id")

    # Initialize
    if method == "initialize":
        return {
            "jsonrpc": "2.0",
            "id": request_id,
            "result": {
                "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
                "capabilities": {"tools": {}},
                "serverInfo": {"name": "my-server", "version": "1.0.0"}
            }
        }

    # List tools
    elif method == "tools/list":
        return {
            "jsonrpc": "2.0",
            "id": request_id,
            "result": {
                "tools": [
                    {
                        "name": "echo",
                        "description": "Echoes back the input message",
                        "inputSchema": {
                            "type": "object",
                            "properties": {
                                "message": {"type": "string", "description": "Message to echo"}
                            },
                            "required": ["message"]
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        "name": "get_time",
                        "description": "Returns current date and time",
                        "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}
                    }
                ]
            }
        }

    # Call tool
    elif method == "tools/call":
        tool_name = params.get("name", "")
        arguments = params.get("arguments", {})

        if tool_name == "echo":
            message = arguments.get("message", "")
            result_text = f"Echo: {message}"
        elif tool_name == "get_time":
            result_text = f"Current time: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}"
        else:
            return {
                "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id,
                "error": {"code": -32601, "message": f"Unknown tool: {tool_name}"}
            }

        return {
            "jsonrpc": "2.0",
            "id": request_id,
            "result": {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": result_text}]}
        }

    # Unknown method
    else:
        return {
            "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id,
            "error": {"code": -32601, "message": f"Method not found: {method}"}
        }


def main():
    """Main loop - read requests from stdin, send responses to stdout."""
    for line in sys.stdin:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            request = json.loads(line)
            response = handle_request(request)
            send_response(response)
        except Exception as e:
            send_response({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": None, "error": {"code": -32603, "message": str(e)}})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Register in mcp.json

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-server": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["path/to/my_server.py"]

}

docs.title: Use Your Server
docs.text:
> echo hello world
> what time is it?

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Startup → Load .quasar/mcp.json → Launch Servers → Discover Tools → Ready
  1. QUASAR reads .quasar/mcp.json on startup
  2. Launches each MCP server as a subprocess
  3. Sends initialize and tools/list requests
  4. Makes discovered tools available to the AI

  • For Python scripts, use relative paths from workspace

docs.title: Session Memory
docs.text: QUASAR maintains session memory to track history and context.

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
.quasar/
└── memory.json    # Session history

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
{
  "history": [
    {
      "timestamp": "2024-02-08T10:30:00",
      "query": "create a hello.py file",

    },

docs.title: What's Stored
docs.text: Field Description history Recent query/summary pairs recent_files Recently accessed files timestamp When each action occurred

docs.title: How It's Used
docs.text:
QUASAR uses memory for:

  1. Context Building: Recent history helps AI understand ongoing work
  2. File Access: Prioritizes recently touched files
  3. Continuity: Maintains context across sessions

docs.title: Memory Limits
docs.text:
To prevent bloat:

  • History: Last 20 entries
  • Recent files: Last 50 files

Older entries are automatically removed.

docs.title: Clearing Memory
docs.text:
To reset memory:

# Delete the file
rm .quasar/memory.json

# Or empty it
echo '{"history": [], "recent_files": []}' > .quasar/memory.json

docs.title: Git Ignore
docs.text:
Memory is typically not version controlled:

# .gitignore
.quasar/memory.json

This keeps personal session history private.

Check if a command is available on the system.

check_command_available(command: str) -> bool

Example:

> is docker installed?

Output:

✅ docker is available at /usr/bin/docker

or

❌ docker is not found in PATH

docs.title: Why Not Execute Directly?
docs.text:
QUASAR doesn't execute commands automatically for safety:

Risk Example Data loss rm -rf / Side effects npm publish Security curl | sh Resource usage fork bomb

By suggesting instead of executing, you maintain control.

docs.title: Shell Integration
docs.text:
You can copy suggested commands directly to your shell:

# QUASAR suggests:
pytest tests/ -v

# You copy and run it yourself

Or use your shell's history:

# After running, it's in your history
!!  # Repeat last command

docs.title: Web Tools
docs.text: 7 tools for web search and URL fetching.

docs.title: tavily_search
docs.text:
Search the web using Tavily API.

tavily_search(query: str, max_results: int = 5) -> str

Examples:

> search for "Python async best practices"
> find tutorials on FastAPI

API Key Required

Set TAVILY_API_KEY in your .env file. Get a free key at tavily.com

docs.title: duckduckgo_search
docs.text:
Search using DuckDuckGo (no API key needed).

duckduckgo_search(query: str, max_results: int = 5) -> str

Example:

> search DuckDuckGo for "Python logging"

docs.title: jina_reader
docs.text:
Extract clean content from a webpage.

jina_reader(url: str) -> str

Example:

> read the content of https://example.com/article

Returns: Clean, formatted text content.

docs.title: fetch_url_content
docs.text:
Fetch raw content from any URL.

fetch_url_content(url: str) -> str

Example:

> fetch https://api.example.com/data.json

docs.title: wikipedia_search
docs.text:
Search Wikipedia articles.

wikipedia_search(query: str) -> str

Example:

> search Wikipedia for "Machine Learning"

docs.title: arxiv_search
docs.text:
Search arXiv for academic papers.

arxiv_search(query: str, max_results: int = 5) -> str

Example:

> find papers on "transformer architecture"

docs.title: github_search
docs.text:
Search GitHub repositories and code.

github_search(query: str, search_type: str = "repositories") -> str

Search Types:

  • repositories - Find repos
  • code - Find code snippets

Example:

> search GitHub for Python CLI frameworks

docs.title: Fallback Behavior
docs.text:
QUASAR tries multiple web tools in sequence:

1. Tavily (if API key)
2. DuckDuckGo
3. Jina Reader

If one fails, it automatically tries the next.
